To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 1-β-alanine substitution in the N-terminus of the corticotropin (1-23)-triketopeptide amide 1b leads to an increase in biological activity of about 500%, whereas the 4-L-methionine to L-leucine substitution in this compound results in a decrease in biological activity to about 50% of 1b.

the N-terminal amino group of the corticotropin-(23–39)-trikosapeptide amide is essential for the biological activity, but that the N-terminal sequence of the corticotopin-(1– 23)-trikoseptide is not.

the N‐terminal amino‐group of corticotropin‐trikosapeptide‐amide (1b) is not essential for the biological activity, and that the replacement of L‐serine by β‐alanine in 1b leads to the most potent analog (1d) with a biological activity about five times higher than that of 1b.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a series of analogs of the N-terminal tripeptide-amid of corticotropin.
the preparation of synthetic analogues of corticotropin (ACTH) and the determination of their biological activities.
the synthesis of analogs of ACTH(1-23)-tripeptidamide (I) and with the study of the structure-activity relationships in these peptides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the synthesis of the 1-β-alanin analogue (1d) is a more efficient method for the preparation of the corticotropic hormone than that of the 1-L-proline analogue (1c), which, however, is a better starting material for the synthesis of the more potent corticotropic hormones.
there is no evidence of a causal relationship between the use of the contraceptive pill and breast cancer.
the synthetic analogues of corticotropin, which have been synthesized up to the present time, have not yet been able to compete with the natural hormone in respect to biological activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have succeeded in synthesising a number of analogues of the N-terminal decapeptide of corticotropin, and have found a number of analogs of this peptide with biological activities which are comparable with that of the parent compound.
the synthesis of a series of analogues with the aim of obtaining a more potent and stable compound than the original one has been achieved.
we have succeeded in synthesizing a series of analogues of the corticotropin-(23–41) fragment, in which the amino acid sequence 1–10 was varied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in addition to its role in the formation of the active conformation, the N-terminal amino group of corticotropin plays a role in the binding process.
we have developed a new approach for the synthesis of 2-alkyl-2-aryl-1,3-dioxanes.
the synthesis of the peptide is a key step in the development of new drugs.
